title: SCOBY food-additive E262 boundary, technical-acetate separation, and zero-waste value hypothesis
scope: Separate technical acetate research from any food-additive pathway and record the potential resource-recovery value of SCOBY-derived acetate without claiming that a home-produced salt is food-grade or E262-compliant.

food_grade_E262.identity_requirement: Must meet applicable official specification for sodium acetate.
food_grade_E262.quality_requirement: Identity, assay, water/hydrate state, and impurity limits must be demonstrated analytically; microbiological and process controls must be appropriate to the intended food use.
food_grade_E262.home_production_claim: A home-made crystalline sodium acetate cannot be called certified food additive E262 merely because its chemistry is nominally sodium acetate.

codex_context.notes: Codex GSFA lists sodium acetate as INS 262(i) with category-specific provisions; permitted uses and levels depend on jurisdiction and food category.
codex_context.source: FAO Codex GSFA Online, updated through the 48th CAC session (2025)

sco_by_product_value.resource_recovery_hypothesis: SCOBY culture can be treated as a multifunctional biological platform in which the same production system may yield a beverage/fermentation product, bacterial cellulose biomass and acetate-rich process liquor. Recovering acetate can therefore reduce the fraction of process carbon leaving the system as an unvalued side stream.
not_admitted: economic superiority to industrial sodium acetate
required_validation: economic assessment where claims of advantage are made

value_chain_hypothesis.principle: Prefer cascading use of biomass and process streams where quality and safety specifications permit, rather than assuming every output must be discarded.

gate_3_specification_conformance.rule: No E262 label or food-grade claim until the complete applicable specification is demonstrated.

technical_acetate_gate.identity: Verify sodium acetate by appropriate analytical methods.
technical_acetate_gate.purity: Report measured assay and relevant impurities; do not use the term food-grade.
technical_acetate_gate.mass_balance: Record acetate generated, sodium-base input, isolated solid, mother liquor and losses.

health_boundary.acetate_metabolism: Acetate can be converted to acetyl-CoA in mammalian metabolism, but this mechanistic fact does not establish a simple or universal pathway from kombucha acetate intake to body-fat gain.

strengths: integrates acetate recovery with a biological production platform
can provide research experience in fermentation and downstream recovery
supports cascading use of biomass/process streams
limitations: potentially higher water/energy burden per gram recovered
depends on established industrial feedstocks and process infrastructure
does not by itself valorize a local SCOBY side stream

comparison_with_industrial_E262.claim_ceiling: The SCOBY route is not admitted as a replacement for industrial E262 production without quantitative comparison of yield, cost, water, energy, waste and specification compliance.

necessity_claim_boundary.allowed_statement: Acetate recovery strengthens the case for studying SCOBY as a multi-output biological platform because it may convert part of an otherwise underused process stream into a measurable chemical product.
necessity_claim_boundary.not_allowed_statement: SCOBY production is necessary because it is a zero-waste or universally environmentally superior route to acetate.

critical_corrections_to_supplied_claims: A home-produced sodium acetate cannot be represented as certified E262 without specification and regulatory compliance.
Boiling or simple recrystallization does not by itself establish food-grade microbiological or chemical purity.
Human tasting must never be used as a process endpoint or safety test for a research-produced salt.
The term 'sterilization' must not be used to imply validated aseptic manufacture without an appropriate validated process.
E262 is a regulatory identity/specification category, not merely a molecular formula.
The environmental benefit of acetate recovery is a hypothesis until energy, water, waste and co-product data are measured.

references.title: EU Regulation 231/2012: specifications for food additives, including E262(i) sodium acetate

next_gate: KEEP_TECHNICAL_ACETATE_AND_FOOD-GRADE_E262_PATHS_SEPARATE; MEASURE ACETATE RECOVERY, PURITY, ENERGY, WATER AND WASTE BALANCE; ONLY AFTER SPECIFICATION AND REGULATORY GATES ARE MET MAY A FOOD-GRADE CLAIM BE CONSIDERED.
authority_rule: This record establishes a boundary and resource-recovery hypothesis. It does not certify any SCOBY-derived product as food-grade E262 and does not establish universal environmental or economic superiority.
